opening.argument: The presentation is structured around explaining Microsoft Teams and its ordinary workplace functionality. It introduces the subject by promising to cover “the core aspects and core functionality of Microsoft Teams,” then demonstrates a workplace collaboration hub with chat, meetings, calling, app integration, colleague search, guest access, administration, and spreadsheet sharing. The visible Teams interfaces reinforce that focus, showing teams, channels, chat, navigation, member addition, and a “Who” tool for finding people with relevant knowledge. The discussion of a “complete meeting and calling solution” and the explanation that “There are different ways how you can use apps in Teams” present product features rather than any request for payment, credentials, or investment participation. Even the administrator instruction to use the Teams portal and log in with an Office 365 account is an ordinary product-start and administration step within a hosted software tutorial.

citations.quote: Let's catch everyone up on the core aspects and core functionality of Microsoft Teams.
There are different ways how you can use apps in Teams.
We've now started to bring all the Skype for Business Online capabilities into Teams to give you a complete meeting and calling solution.
Simply go to the link shown. And if you're an admin and you want to try the first version of the new Admin Center,. Please go to admin.teams.microsoft.com and log in with your Office 365 account.
